decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm mouse approach: lift into elbow-up reach and gradually pitch the open gripper downward. Mouse position estimated from calibrated head view.
Continue above the red mouse with a near-vertical open grasp, preserving the established elbow-up branch.
Lower the right gripper over the mouse, compensating fingertip offset as the wrist becomes vertical and aligning with its angled body.
Fine-adjust toward the mouse center using the wrist view, close fully, and make a short test lift to check retention visually.
Lift the apparently retained mouse and translate right over the black pad; keep the grasp fully closed and verify alignment before release.
Set the mouse down on the pad, open the right gripper, and lift clear. The mouse is visibly retained and centered over the pad.
Mouse rests on the pad. Retract the right arm and raise the left arm into a continuous elbow-up approach for a two-point keyboard push.
Bring closed grippers behind the keyboard front edge at two separated contact points. Lower gradually with downward pitch, keeping arms on their own sides.
Advance slowly to engage the keyboard front edge with both closed grippers; bring the right contact slightly inward and check actual sliding.
Keyboard has not visibly translated yet. Back off slightly, lower the closed fingertip contacts to its front rim, then re-engage gently.
Keyboard now slides. Relieve slight downward contact and push both contact points forward-right toward the outlined frame without crossing arms.
Continue the coordinated shallow keyboard push toward the frame. Limit left-arm lateral travel to remain left of the midline; inspect alignment after this increment.
Keyboard appears aligned over its frame. Open and withdraw both hands, lifting clear; move the left hand toward a figurine approach while keeping the right arm out of the way.
Position the open left gripper above and in front of the figurine for a torso grasp. Retract the right arm toward its home region without crossing workspaces.
The figurine has tipped. Reposition above its lying torso with a vertical open grasp while retaining clearance, rather than continuing the original approach; settle the right arm near home.
Lift clear of the fallen figurine, then align above its torso with the jaws turning across its body. Its pose changed during the prior approach, so re-center from the latest views.
Descend cautiously toward the lying figurine's torso while completing the cross-body jaw alignment. Use the head view to correct the forward offset.
The figurine shifted under the open fingers. Lift slightly, center the jaws farther over its torso, then close for a test grasp without dragging along the table.
Make a slow vertical test lift with the left gripper fully closed. Verify whether the figurine follows before attempting transport or reorientation.
The test lift did not retain the figurine. Reopen, shift from the legs toward the torso, and descend closer to the table for a lower grasp.
The torso is now between the jaws in the wrist view. Lower a final small amount, close fully, and make another short retention test lift.
Previous closure was above or offset from the torso. Reopen, correct inward toward its visible center, and lower the grasp plane before closing again.
The jaws now enclose the figurine's chest. Lift slowly with full closure and verify retention before rotating the fallen figure upright.
The figure remained on the table after lifting. Correct the grasp height downward and re-center over the chest with open jaws; the previous closure appears to have been above the body.
Relieve the low-contact tracking error, then use wrist-image centering to move the open jaws from the head toward the torso before another closure.
The waist is centered across the open jaws. Lower slightly, close fully at the waist, and test a small lift while checking the head view for actual object motion.
Re-estimate the torso grasp from calibrated head geometry rather than apparent wrist overlap. Reopen and lower the actual grasp plane while shifting slightly forward.
Relieve table contact and correct the lateral jaw offset seen in the wrist image. Close around the torso at this height and test retention with a small lift.
The figurine is still not retained. Open and lift clear, then move toward the upright alarm clock; revisit the figurine after securing the easier placement.
Approach above the alarm clock with open jaws across its sides, maintaining clearance over the keyboard and the existing elbow-up configuration.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller increments and a slightly lower approach, keeping the elbow-up branch while aligning vertically over the clock.
Lower in place to regain reach margin after the continuity rejection, then advance only a small distance toward the clock. Maintain the elbow-up configuration.
Change to a forward-angled clock grasp instead of extending the vertical wrist farther. Pitch gradually while withdrawing slightly to preserve reach and continuity.
Center the open jaws on the clock's sides, lower slightly, close fully, and test a short lift. The forward-angled approach now has good reach margin.
The fingers closed in front of the clock rather than around it. Reopen, advance the grasp plane onto its sides, then close and test again with small continuous increments.
The clock is now enclosed between the jaws. Lift and retract diagonally left with full closure to verify retention and clear the keyboard before transport to the drawer.
The clock did not follow the lift. Return with open jaws to a deeper side grasp, advancing beyond its front face while keeping the established reachable wrist angle.
Lower onto the clock's sides at the deeper alignment, close fully, and lift vertically without lateral motion to check for secure retention.
The clock remains on the desk and the fingers appear too high. Reopen and lower the side-contact height before another fully closed retention test.
Test the lower clock grasp with a slow lift, then retract slightly for reach margin. Keep full closure and use visible object motion to confirm retention.
Clock visibly follows the hand. Lift it above the drawer lip while moving left and slightly back for reach margin, maintaining its upright orientation and full closure.
The clock slipped during transport and is now beside the drawer. Reopen and approach its new position from above with a vertical grasp, avoiding the drawer wall.
Replan after the continuity rejection: retain the current wrist angle, lower and retract slightly to reduce elbow flexion while aligning over the relocated clock.
The left fingers are close to the drawer wall. Move clear to the right before descending toward the clock, using the latest pose after contact-related tracking error.
Descend from the clear approach to put the finger contact plane on the clock's body, then close fully and make a short vertical test lift.
The closed fingertips remain in front of the clock. Reopen and advance the side-contact region deeper around its body while maintaining height, then close fully.
Clock moved within the jaws on closure. Lift slowly and slightly retract while holding fully closed; establish clearance before any sideways transport past the drawer.
Clock is visibly lifted and retained. Raise it further on the clear side of the drawer, retracting for reach margin; do not traverse the drawer wall until its base clears the top.
Add vertical clearance above the drawer lip before beginning slow leftward transport. Clock remains visibly stable in the closed grasp; preserve wrist orientation.
After the IK interruption, lower and retract slightly to restore reach margin, then translate left in front of the drawer. Keep the retained clock steady and fully gripped.
The previous recovery was rejected without motion. Use submillimeter initial lowering to leave the high-flexion boundary continuously, holding the clock and wrist orientation unchanged.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion. Translate the held clock left along the clear drawer front, retracting for reach margin and adding slight height.
Clock slipped and rests in a nearer reachable area. Switch to a vertical top-down side grasp for better retention, reopening and aligning above its new location.
Lower the vertical open gripper over the face-up clock, correcting its center from the calibrated head view. Stop above the table to inspect side alignment before closing.
Clock is centered under the vertical jaws. Lower to enclose its side walls, close fully, and test a small vertical lift before transport.
Lift the centered clock gradually with full closure and slight retraction. Verify stable retention before moving across the drawer's edge.
Clock is stably retained in the vertical grasp. Raise along the drawer's clear front while gently pitching forward for reach margin, keeping full closure and avoiding the lip.
Carry the retained clock over the drawer's front lip with added height and a gradual forward pitch. Keep the grasp closed and monitor clearance and elbow continuity.
After the continuity interruption, advance with smaller steps while slightly lowering and pitching forward to reduce elbow flexion. Maintain the visible clock grasp and approach the drawer top.
The clock is now above the drawer top. Move slightly inward and lower gently, then open the gripper to leave it on the top surface.
The released clock appears too close to the front lip. Reclose while it remains between the jaws, lift slightly, and move farther inward before another release.
Clock is falling off the front rather than resting on top. Withdraw the empty open hand from the lip and lower continuously out of the high-flexion boundary before reacquiring it.
The preceding retreat was rejected with no motion. Begin with submillimeter lowering and retraction, then ramp gradually away from the high-flexion boundary.
Reacquire the clock at its new resting position beside the drawer. Approach from above with open jaws and a gradual downward pitch, remaining clear of the cabinet wall.
The open jaw is contacting the drawer wall. Retreat slightly forward and right to clear it, then lower with a forward-angled approach to the clock.
Lower the centered open jaws onto the clock's side walls, with a small forward correction, then close fully and begin a minimal lift test.
Lift and slightly retract from the cabinet contact while maintaining closure. Check whether the clock follows; do not infer retention from the gripper command.
The clock did not follow the lift. Change to a vertical grasp with diagonal jaw alignment and shift clear of the drawer wall before descending again.
Lower the vertically aligned open jaws along the clock sides. Diagonal jaw alignment keeps the rear finger to the clear side of the drawer wall.
Relieve the small contact residual, move the open grasp deeper onto the clock's center, and close before a short vertical retention test.
Clear the cabinet contact and reorient the jaws parallel to its side wall. Reopen and lift away before trying a less obstructed clock grasp.
Correct the visible clock offset by moving left and forward while descending. The jaw opening now runs along the cabinet wall rather than into it; inspect before closure.
